questionText: In an office, 76% of the number of females is equal to the one-third of the number of males. What is the ratio of number of males to that of the females in the office?
solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Given, 1/3 of Males = 76% of Females
⇒ M / 3 = (76 / 100) × F
⇒ M / 3 = (19 / 25) × F
⇒ M / F = (19 × 3) / 25 = 57 / 25
∴ The correct answer is 57 : 25.

Alternate Method
Given:
76% of the number of females is equal to^(1/3) of the number of males.

Formula Used:
Percentage value = (Rate ÷ 100) × Base value

Calculations:
Let the total number of males be M and the total number of females be F.
⇒ 76% of F = (1 / 3) × M
⇒ (76 ÷ 100) × F = M ÷ 3
⇒ (19 ÷ 25) × F = M ÷ 3

Rearranging the terms to find the ratio of M to F:

⇒ M ÷ F = (19 ÷ 25) × 3
⇒ M ÷ F = 57 ÷ 25
⇒ M : F = 57 : 25
∴ The correct answer is 57 : 25.

Additional Information
Ratio & Proportion Basics

A ratio compares two quantities of the same kind. The ratio of a to b is written as a : b or a ÷ b. The first term is called the antecedent, and the second term is the consequent.

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

To convert a percentage into a fraction, simply divide the percentage value by 100 and simplify. For example, 76% = 76 ÷ 100 = 19 ÷ 25.

Equivalent Ratios

Multiplying or dividing both terms of a ratio by the same non - zero number does not change the ratio. This property is highly useful to simplify complex fractional equations into simplest form.

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questionText: Ramesh sold his bike for ₹16,384 and incurred a loss of 20%. At what price should he have sold the bike to gain a profit of 30%?
solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Selling Price at 20% loss = 80% of CP = ₹16, 384
Required Selling Price at 30% profit = 130% of CP
New SP = (16384 ÷ 80) × 130
New SP = 204.8 × 130 = ₹26, 624
∴ The correct answer is ₹26, 624.

Alternate Method
Given:
Initial Selling Price (SP1) = ₹16, 384
Loss Percentage = 20%
Required Profit Percentage = 30%

Formula Used:
Cost Price (CP) = SP1 × [100 ÷ (100 - Loss%)]
New Selling Price (SP²) = CP × [(100 + Profit%) ÷ 100]

Calculations:
⇒ CP = 16384 × [100 ÷ (100 - 20)]
⇒ CP = 16384 × (100 ÷ 80)
⇒ CP = 204.8 × 100 = ₹20, 480
⇒ SP² = 20480 × [(100 + 30) ÷ 100]
⇒ SP² = 20480 × (130 ÷ 100)
⇒ SP² = 2048 × 13 = ₹26, 624
∴ The correct answer is ₹26, 624.

Additional Information
Cost Price (CP)

It is the exact price at which goods are originally bought. Profit and loss values are always calculated on the base cost price unless clearly specified otherwise.

Successive Percentage Change

When a value is updated successively by a% and b%, the total net percentage change is given by the formula: (a + b + ab ÷ 100)%.

Marked Price (MP) & Discount

Discount is fundamentally given on the marked price or printed price of the item. Consequently, Selling Price = MP - Discount.

Solution

Shortcut Trick
Convert 67° angles to 23° using cot 67° = tan 23° and sin 67° = cos 23°.
⇒ 2 cosec² 23° tan² 23° - (sin² 23° + cos² 23°) - tan² 23°
⇒ 2(1 / sin² 23°) × (sin² 23° / cos² 23°) - 1 - tan² 23°
⇒ 2 sec² 23° - 1 - tan² 23° = sec² 23° + (sec² 23° - tan² 23°) - 1
⇒ sec² 23° + 1 - 1 = sec² 23°
∴ The correct answer is sec² 23°.

Alternate Method
Given:
2 cosec² 23° cot² 67° - sin² 23° - sin² 67° - cot² 67°

Formulas Used: sin(90° - θ) = cos θ
cot(90° - θ) = tan θ
sin²θ + cos²θ = 1
sec²θ - tan²θ = 1

Calculation:
⇒ 2 cosec² 23° cot2(90° - 23°) - sin² 23° - sin2(90° - 23°) - cot2(90° - 23°)
⇒ 2 cosec² 23° tan² 23° - sin² 23° - cos² 23° - tan² 23°
⇒ 2(1 / sin² 23°) × (sin² 23° / cos² 23°) - (sin² 23° + cos² 23°) - tan² 23°
⇒ 2(1 / cos² 23°) - 1 - tan² 23°
⇒ 2 sec² 23° - 1 - tan² 23°
⇒ sec² 23° + (sec² 23° - tan² 23°) - 1
⇒ sec² 23° + 1 - 1
⇒ sec² 23°
∴ The correct answer is sec² 23°.

Additional Information
Trigonometric Identities

The fundamental Pythagorean identities are sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, sec²θ - tan²θ = 1, and cosec²θ - cot²θ = 1.

Complementary Angles

Two angles are complementary if their sum is 90°. Key relations: sin(90° - θ) = cos θ, tan(90° - θ) = cot θ, and sec(90° - θ) = cosec θ.

Reciprocal Relations

Trigonometric ratios are related by reciprocal identities: cosec θ = 1 / sin θ, sec θ = 1 / cos θ, and cot θ = 1 / tan θ.

questionText: The system of equations: 2x + 3y = 7 and (a - b)x + (a + b)y = 3a + b - 2 have infinitely many solutions:
solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
For infinitely many solutions, the ratio of coefficients must be equal: a1/a² = b1/b².

⇒ 2 / (a - b) = 3 / (a + b)
⇒ 2a + 2b = 3a - 3b ⇒ a = 5b
Check options: Only Option 4 has a = 5 and b = 1, which perfectly satisfies a = 5b.
∴ The correct answer is a = 5, b = 1.

Alternate Method
Given:
2x + 3y = 7
(a - b)x + (a + b)y = 3a + b - 2

Formula Used:
For a system of equations to have infinitely many solutions, the ratio of their coefficients must be equal: a1 / a² = b1 / b² = c1 / c²

Calculations:
⇒ Here, a1 = 2, b1 = 3, c1 = 7
⇒ a² = (a - b), b² = (a + b), c² = (3a + b - 2)
⇒ 2 / (a - b) = 3 / (a + b) = 7 / (3a + b - 2)
⇒ Equating the first two parts:
⇒ 2 / (a - b) = 3 / (a + b)
⇒ 2(a + b) = 3(a - b)
⇒ 2a + 2b = 3a - 3b
⇒ a = 5b --- (Equation 1)
⇒ Equating the second and third parts:
⇒ 3 / (a + b) = 7 / (3a + b - 2)
⇒ 3(3a + b - 2) = 7(a + b)
⇒ 9a + 3b - 6 = 7a + 7b
⇒ 2a - 4b = 6
⇒ a - 2b = 3 --- (Equation 2)
⇒ Substituting a = 5b into Equation 2:
⇒ 5b - 2b = 3
⇒ 3b = 3 ⇒ b = 1
⇒ Substitute b = 1 back into Equation 1:
⇒ a = 5 × 1 = 5
∴ The correct answer is a = 5, b = 1.

Additional Information
Unique Solution

A system of linear equations has a unique solution if the lines intersect at exactly one point. The condition is a1 / a² = ̸ b1 / b².

No Solution

A system of equations has no solution if the lines are parallel and never intersect. The condition is a1 / a² = b1 / b² = ̸ c1 / c².

Infinitely Many Solutions

A system of equations has infinitely many solutions if the lines overlap entirely, meaning they represent the exact same line. The condition is a1 / a² = b1 / b² = c1 / c².

questionText: In a government scheme, if an electricity bill is paid before due date, one gets a reduction of 13.5% on the amount of the bill. By paying the bill before due date, Ritu got a reduction of Rs. 6,075. The amount of her electricity bill was:
solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
13.5% of Bill Amount = Rs. 6075
1% of Bill Amount = 6075 ÷ 13.5 = 450
100% of Bill Amount = 450 × 100 = 45000
∴ The correct answer is Rs. 45, 000.

Alternate Method
Given:
Reduction percentage = 13.5%
Amount of reduction = Rs. 6075

Formula Used:
Percentage Value = (Percentage ÷ 100) × Base Value

Calculations:
Let the total amount of the electricity bill be x.
⇒ 13.5% of x = 6075
⇒ (13.5 ÷ 100) × x = 6075
⇒ x = (6075 × 100) ÷ 13.5
⇒ x = 607500 ÷ 13.5
⇒ x = 6075000 ÷ 135
⇒ x = 45000
∴ The correct answer is Rs. 45, 000.

Additional Information
Base and Percentage Relationship

When a specific percentage of a base value is given, the complete base value can be found directly using the relation: Base = (Given Value × 100) ÷ Percentage Rate.

Percentage Increase or Decrease

New Value = Original Value × (1 ± r ÷ 100), where r is the percentage rate of change.

Successive Percentage Change

If an amount is subjected to two successive percentage changes of a% and b%, the net effective change is calculated as: (a + b + ab ÷ 100)%.

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questionText: A man sells 10 pens for ₹18 gaining 24%. How many pens should he sell for ₹1,530 to earn a profit of 55%?
solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Using the proportional ratio: (Amount ÷ Quantity) ÷ (100 + Profit%) = Constant
⇒ (18 ÷ 10) ÷ 124 = (1530 ÷ N) ÷ 155
⇒ 1.8 ÷ 124 = 1530 ÷ (155 × N)
⇒ N = (1530 × 124) ÷ (1.8 × 155)
⇒ N = 680
∴ The correct answer is 680 pens.

Alternate Method
Given:
Selling Price (SP1) of 10 pens = ₹18
Initial Profit = 24%
Target Profit = 55%
Target Amount = ₹1530

Formula Used:
CP = SP × [100 ÷ (100 + Profit%)]
New SP = CP × [(100 + New Profit%) ÷ 100]

Calculations:
⇒ SP1 of 1 pen = 18 ÷ 10 = ₹1.80
⇒ CP of 1 pen = 1.80 × (100 ÷ 124) = ₹45/31
⇒ Target SP² of 1 pen for 55% profit = CP × (155 ÷ 100)
⇒ Target SP² = (45 ÷ 31) × (155 ÷ 100)
⇒ Target SP² = 45 × (5 ÷ 100) = ₹2.25
⇒ Number of pens = Total Amount ÷ Target SP²
⇒ Number of pens = 1530 ÷ 2.25
⇒ Number of pens = 680
∴ The correct answer is 680 pens.

Additional Information
Marked Price and Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). Formula: SP = MP × [1 - (Discount% ÷ 100)].

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the effective single discount is (a + b - ab ÷ 100)%.

Dishonest Dealer

When a dealer sells goods at cost price but uses a false weight, the actual Profit% = [Error ÷ (True Value - Error)] × 100.

questionText: The average runs made by a batsman in 10 innings of cricket was 43. How many runs does he have to make in the next inning so that the average of his runs increases by 3?
solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Using the average deviation method to find the required runs directly: Runs required = Old average + (Total new innings × Increase in average)

Runs required = 43 + (11 × 3)
Runs required = 43 + 33 = 76
∴ The correct answer is 76 runs.

Alternate Method
Given:
Average runs in the first 10 innings = 43
Required increase in average = 3

Formula Used:
Average = Sum of all observations ÷ Total number of observations
Total 11 Innings → New Average: 46
10 Innings (Avg = 43)
11th = ?
Deviation: 10 innings need + 3 runs each
11th Inning = 46 + (10 × 3) = 76

Calculations:
⇒ Total runs scored in 10 innings = 10 × 43 = 430 runs
⇒ Target new average for 11 innings = 43 + 3 = 46 runs
⇒ Total runs required in 11 innings = 11 × 46 = 506 runs
⇒ Runs required in the 11th inning = Total runs in 11 innings - Total runs in 10 innings
⇒ Runs required = 506 - 430 = 76
∴ The correct answer is 76 runs.

Additional Information
Basic Average Concept

The average of any set of values is formulated as: Average = Sum of all values ÷ Total count of values.

Deviation Method for Included Items

When a new item is added to a group, its value can be quickly found without large calculations using: Value of added item = Old Average + (Total new items × Change in Average).

Combined Average

When two groups of sizes n1 and n² with averages A1 and A² respectively are merged, the combined average is calculated as: (n1A1 + n2A²) ÷ (n1 + n²).

questionText: 2 tables and 3 chairs together cost ₹12000. When the cost of a table is decreased by 10% and that of a chair is increased by 20%, then 3 tables and 4 chairs together cost ₹17100. What is the total original cost of 1 table and 2 chairs?
solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Let T and C be the original cost of a table and a chair.
Given: 2T + 3C = 12000 ⇒ (1) and 3(0.9T) + 4(1.2C) = 17100 ⇒ 9T + 16C = 57000 ⇒ (2)
Applying 16 × (1) - 3 × (2): 32T - 27T = 192000 - 171000 ⇒ 5T = 21000 ⇒ T = 4200.
Substitute T = 4200 in (1) to get 2(4200) + 3C = 12000 ⇒ 3C = 3600 ⇒ C = 1200.
Required cost = 1 Table + 2 Chairs = 4200 + 2(1200) = ₹6600.
∴ The correct answer is ₹6600.

Alternate Method
Let the original cost of a table be T and a chair be C.
⇒ 2T + 3C = 12000 ...... (Equation 1)
Cost of a table decreased by 10% and cost of a chair increased by 20%.

According to the new condition:

⇒ 3 × (0.9T) + 4 × (1.2C) = 17100
⇒ 2.7T + 4.8C = 17100

Divide the equation by 3:

⇒ 0.9T + 1.6C = 5700

Multiply the equation by 10:

⇒ 9T + 16C = 57000 ...... (Equation 2)

Multiply Equation 1 by 16 and Equation 2 by 3:

⇒ 32T + 48C = 192000
⇒ 27T + 48C = 171000

Subtract the two modified equations:

⇒ 5T = 21000
⇒ T = 4200
Substitute T = 4200 in Equation 1:
⇒ 2 × 4200 + 3C = 12000
⇒ 8400 + 3C = 12000
⇒ 3C = 3600
⇒ C = 1200

The total original cost of 1 table and 2 chairs:

⇒ T + 2C = 4200 + 2 × 1200 = 4200 + 2400 = 6600
∴ The correct answer is ₹6600.

Additional Information
Percentage Change

When a value is increased or decreased by x%, the new value becomes (1 ± x/100) × Original Value.

Linear Equations in Two Variables

These can be solved using substitution, elimination, or cross - multiplication to find unique values of unknown variables.

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questionText: If 2 men or 4 women or 6 boys can finish a work in 50 days, then how many days will 1 man, 1 woman and 1 boy take to finish the same work?
solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Time = Given Days ÷ [ (Mand / Mor) + (Wand / Wor) + (Band / Bor) ]
Time = 50 ÷ [ (1 / 2) + (1 / 4) + (1 / 6) ]
Time = 50 ÷ [ (6 + 3 + 2) / 12 ]
Time = 50 × (12 / 11) = 600 / 11
∴ The correct answer is 54 6/11 days.

Alternate Method
Given:
⇒ 2 men complete work in 50 days ⇒ 1 man takes 2 × 50 = 100 days
⇒ 4 women complete work in 50 days ⇒ 1 woman takes 4 × 50 = 200 days
⇒ 6 boys complete work in 50 days ⇒ 1 boy takes 6 × 50 = 300 days

Person Days Total Work Efficiency

1 Man 100 600 6

1 Woman 200 3

1 Boy 300 2

Calculations:
⇒ Combined efficiency of 1 man, 1 woman, and 1 boy = 6 + 3 + 2 = 11 units/day
⇒ Time taken = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency
⇒ Time taken = 600 ÷ 11 = 54 6/11 days
∴ The correct answer is 54 6/11 days.

Additional Information
AND / OR Rule in Time & Work

When a question states that A OR B can do a work in D days, the time taken by A AND B together is calculated by dividing the given days by the sum of ratios of required workers to given workers.

MDH Concept

For group work problems, use the formula M1 × D1 × H1 / W1 = M² × D² × H² / W², where M is men, D is days, H is hours, and W is work.
Total Work & Efficiency

Total Work is always equal to the Efficiency (amount of work done per unit time) multiplied by the Total Time taken to complete the job.

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questionText: If the area of the base of a right circular cone is 157 cm2 and its slant height is \sqrt{491} cm, then the volume of the cone is _______ (Use π = 3.14).
solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Given Base Area = 157 cm², so π × r² = 157 ⇒ r² = 157 ÷ 3.14 = 50.
Height h = √(l² - r²) = √(491 - 50) = √441 = 21 cm.
Volume of cone = (1/3) × Base Area × Height.
Volume = (1/3) × 157 × 21 = 157 × 7 = 1099 cm³.
∴ The correct answer is 1099 cm³.

Alternate Method
Given:
Base area of the cone = 157 cm²
Slant height (l) = √491 cm
(π = 3.14)

Formula Used:
Area of base = π × r²

Calculations:
⇒ Area of base = π × r² = 157
⇒ 3.14 × r² = 157
⇒ r² = 157 ÷ 3.14 = 50
⇒ We know that, l² = r² + h²
⇒ (√491)2 = 50 + h²
⇒ 491 = 50 + h²
⇒ h² = 491 - 50 = 441
⇒ h = √441 = 21 cm
⇒ Volume of the cone = 1/3 × π × r² × h
⇒ Volume = 1/3 × (3.14 × 50) × 21
⇒ Volume = 1/3 × 157 × 21
⇒ Volume = 157 × 7 = 1099 cm³
∴ The correct answer is 1099 cm³.

Additional Information
Volume of a Cone vs Cylinder

A cone's volume is exactly one - third of the volume of a cylinder with the same base radius and height. The formula is V = 1/3 × πr2h.

Surface Area of a Cone

The curved surface area is given by πrl and the total surface area is given by πr(r + l), where r is the radius and l is the slant height.

Frustum of a Cone

When a cone is sliced parallel to its base, the remaining lower part is called a frustum. Its volume is^(1/3) × πh(R² + r² + Rr).

questionText: P, Q, R and S are four points on a circle. PR and QS intersect at a point X such that ∠QXR = 120° and ∠XRS = 10°. The measure of ∠QPR is:
solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
In ΔSXR, the exterior angle is equal to the sum of the two opposite interior angles.

⇒ ∠QXR = ∠XSR + ∠XRS
⇒ 120° = ∠XSR + 10° ⇒ ∠XSR = 110°

Angles subtended by the same arc (QR) in the same segment of a circle are equal.

⇒ ∠QPR = ∠QSR = ∠XSR = 110°
∴ The correct answer is 110°.

Alternate Method
Given:
⇒ ∠QXR = 120°
⇒ ∠XRS = 10°

Formula Used:
⇒ Linear pair sum = 180°
⇒ Sum of angles in a triangle = 180°
⇒ Angles subtended by the same arc at the circumference are equal.

Q / P

S / R

X

120°

10°

Calculations:
⇒ Since QS is a straight line segment, ∠SXR and ∠QXR form a linear pair.
⇒ ∠SXR + ∠QXR = 180°
⇒ ∠SXR = 180° - 120° = 60°
⇒ In ΔSXR, the sum of all interior angles is 180°.
⇒ ∠XSR + ∠SXR + ∠XRS = 180°
⇒ ∠XSR + 60° + 10° = 180°
⇒ ∠XSR = 180° - 70° = 110°
⇒ We know that angles subtended by the same arc at the circumference are equal.
⇒ Therefore, ∠QPR and ∠QSR (which is the same as ∠XSR) subtending the same arc QR must be equal.
⇒ ∠QPR = ∠QSR = 110°
∴ The correct answer is 110°.

Additional Information
Angles in the Same Segment

Angles subtended by the same arc at any point on the remaining part of the circle are always equal.

Exterior Angle Theorem

The measure of an exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the measures of its two remote interior angles.

Cyclic Quadrilateral

A quadrilateral formed by four points on a circle is called a cyclic quadrilateral. The sum of its opposite interior angles is always 180°.

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questionText: What is the slope of the line whose equation is x + 2y = 4?
solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
For a standard linear equation of the form Ax + By = C, the slope is directly given by - A / B.
Given equation: x + 2y = 4
Here, the coefficient of x is A = 1 and the coefficient of y is B = 2.
Slope = -1 / 2.
∴ The correct answer is - 1/2.

Alternate Method
Given:
The equation of the line: x + 2y = 4

Formula Used:
The slope - intercept form of a line is y = mx + c, where 'm' represents the slope and 'c' represents the y - intercept.

Calculations:
⇒ We need to express the given equation in the slope - intercept form (y = mx + c).
⇒ Start with the given equation: x + 2y = 4
⇒ Subtract x from both sides to isolate the y term:
⇒ 2y = -x + 4
⇒ Divide the entire equation by 2 to solve for y:
⇒ y = (-1/2)x + (4/2)
⇒ y = (-1/2)x + 2
⇒ By comparing this result with y = mx + c, we can identify that the slope m is - 1/2 and the y - intercept c is 2.
∴ The correct answer is - 1/2.

Additional Information
Slope of a Line (Gradient)

The slope measures the steepness and direction of a line. It is calculated as the change in y divided by the change in x. Formula: m = (y² - y1) ÷ (x² - x1).

X and Y Intercepts

The x - intercept is the point where the line crosses the horizontal x - axis (where y = 0). The y - intercept is the point where it crosses the vertical y - axis (where x = 0).

Parallel and Perpendicular Lines

Two parallel lines always have equal slopes (m1 = m²). Two perpendicular lines have slopes that are negative reciprocals of each other (m1 × m² = -1).

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questionText: The average of the first five multiples of 3 is:
solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
The multiples of any number form an Arithmetic Progression (A.P.).

For an A.P. with an odd number of terms, the average is exactly the middle term.

The middle term of the first 5 multiples is the 3rd multiple.

⇒ Average = 3 × 3 = 9
∴ The correct answer is 9.

Alternate Method
Given:
The sequence consists of the first five multiples of 3.

Formula Used:
Average = Sum of all observations ÷ Total number of observations

Calculations:
⇒ The first five multiples of 3 are: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15.
⇒ Sum of these multiples = 3 + 6 + 9 + 12 + 15
⇒ Sum = 45
⇒ Total number of multiples = 5
⇒ Average = 45 ÷ 5
⇒ Average = 9
∴ The correct answer is 9.

Additional Information
Average of an Arithmetic Progression (A.P.)

For any sequence in A.P., the average can also be calculated directly using the formula: (First Term + Last Term) ÷ 2. Here, it is (3 + 15) ÷ 2 = 9.

Average of first n multiples of a number k

The direct shortcut formula to find the average of the first n multiples of a number k is k × (n + 1) ÷ 2. Here, it is 3 × (5 + 1) ÷ 2 = 9.

Average of first n natural numbers

The average of the first n consecutive natural numbers is given by the formula (n + 1) ÷ 2.

questionText: A invests ₹8,000 and B invests ₹11,000 at the same rate of simple interest per annum. If, at the end of 3 years, B gets ₹720 more interest than A, then find the rate of simple interest per annum.
solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Difference in principal between B and A = ₹11, 000 - ₹8, 000 = ₹3, 000.

Extra simple interest generated by this additional ₹3, 000 in 3 years = ₹720.

Extra simple interest for 1 year = ₹720 ÷ 3 = ₹240.
Rate of interest = (Interest for 1 year ÷ Extra Principal) × 100
Rate = (240 ÷ 3000) × 100 = 8%.
∴ The correct answer is 8%.

Alternate Method
Given:
Principal of A (PA) = ₹8, 000
Principal of B (PB) = ₹11, 000
Time (T) = 3 years
Difference in Interest (SIB - SIA) = ₹720

Formula Used:
Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100
A's Principal: ₹8, 000
B's Principal: ₹11, 000 + ₹3, 000
Extra Interest in 3 yrs = ₹720 → Rate = 8%

Calculations:
⇒ Let the uniform rate of interest be R% per annum.
⇒ Interest received by B = (11000 × R × 3) ÷ 100 = 330R
⇒ Interest received by A = (8000 × R × 3) ÷ 100 = 240R
⇒ Difference in Interest = 330R - 240R
⇒ 90R = 720
⇒ R = 720 ÷ 90
⇒ R = 8
∴ The correct answer is 8%.

Additional Information
Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

Simple Interest is calculated only on the initial principal amount throughout the entire period, while Compound Interest is calculated on both the principal and the accumulated interest from previous periods.

Compound Interest Formula

A = P(1 + R ÷ 100)T, where A is the total amount, P is the principal, R is the rate of interest, and T is the time period.
Difference between CI and SI for 2 years
Difference = P × (R ÷ 100)2

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questionText: A diver rowing at the speed of 3 km/h in still water takes double the time going 50 km upstream compared to going 50 km downstream. The speed of the diver against the stream is
solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Since the distance (50 km) is constant, the speed of the diver is inversely proportional to the time taken.

Time ratio (Upstream : Downstream) = 2 : 1 ⇒ Speed ratio (Upstream : Downstream) = 1 : 2
Speed in still water = (Upstream Speed + Downstream Speed) ÷ 2 = (1 + 2) ÷ 2 = 1.5 ratio units.

We are given that still water speed is 3 km/h ⇒ 1.5 ratio units = 3 km/h.

⇒ 1 ratio unit = 2 km/h. Since the upstream speed corresponds to 1 ratio unit, it directly equals 2 km/h.
∴ The correct answer is 2 km/h.

Alternate Method
Given:
Speed of diver in still water (v) = 3 km/h
Distance traveled upstream and downstream = 50 km
Time taken upstream = 2 × Time taken downstream

Formula Used:
Time = Distance ÷ Speed
Upstream Speed = v - s | Downstream Speed = v + s

Calculations:
Let the speed of the stream be s km/h.
⇒ Upstream speed (U) = (3 - s) km/h
⇒ Downstream speed (D) = (3 + s) km/h

According to the given condition in the question:

⇒ 50 ÷ (3 - s) = 2 × [50 ÷ (3 + s)]

Canceling 50 from both sides:

⇒ 1 ÷ (3 - s) = 2 ÷ (3 + s)

By cross - multiplying:

⇒ 3 + s = 2 × (3 - s)
⇒ 3 + s = 6 - 2s
⇒ s + 2s = 6 - 3
⇒ 3s = 3
⇒ s = 1 km/h

The speed of the diver against the stream (Upstream Speed):

⇒ U = 3 - s
⇒ U = 3 - 1 = 2 km/h.
∴ The correct answer is 2 km/h.

Additional Information
Speed in Still Water

It is the average of the downstream and upstream speeds. Formula: v = (D + U) ÷ 2, where D is downstream speed and U is upstream speed.

Speed of Stream

It is half the difference between the downstream and upstream speeds. Formula: s = (D - U) ÷ 2.

Constant Distance Relation

Whenever the distance traveled is constant, the ratio of speeds is always inversely proportional to the ratio of their respective times taken. (Speed ∝ 1 ÷ Time).
conceptTested: Relationship between speed in still water, upstream speed, and downstream speed when distance is constant.

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questionText: The radius of a cylinder is 5 cm more than its height. If the curved surface area of the cylinder is 792 cm², then the volume of the cylinder (in cm³), is ________. [Use \(\pi = \frac{22}{7}\) ]
solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 2 × π × r × h = 792 ⇒ π × r × h = 396
Volume of a cylinder is π × r² × h = (π × r × h) × r = 396 × Rs. ince 2 × (22/7) × r × (r - 5) = 792 ⇒ r × (r - 5) = 126
By simple observation, 14 × (14 - 5) = 126, so the radius r = 14 cm
Volume = 396 × 14 = 5544 cm³
∴ The correct answer is 5544 cm³.

Alternate Method
Given:
Radius of cylinder (r) = height (h) + 5
Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 792 cm²

Formula Used:
Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 2 × π × r × h
Volume of cylinder = π × r² × h

Calculation:
⇒ 2 × (22/7) × (h + 5) × h = 792
⇒ (44/7) × (h² + 5h) = 792
⇒ h² + 5h = 792 × 7 ÷ 44
⇒ h² + 5h = 18 × 7
⇒ h² + 5h - 126 = 0
⇒ h² + 14h - 9h - 126 = 0
⇒ h(h + 14) - 9(h + 14) = 0
⇒ (h - 9)(h + 14) = 0
⇒ h = 9 cm (since height cannot be negative)
⇒ Radius (r) = 9 + 5 = 14 cm
⇒ Volume = (22/7) × (14)² × 9
⇒ Volume = (22/7) × 196 × 9 = 22 × 28 × 9
⇒ Volume = 616 × 9 = 5544 cm³
∴ The correct answer is 5544 cm³.

Additional Information
Properties of a Cylinder

A cylinder is a 3D solid with two parallel circular bases. Total Surface Area (TSA) = CSA + 2 × Base Area = 2 × π × r × (r + h).

Volume of Related Shapes

The volume of a cone with the same base radius and height as a cylinder is exactly one - third of the cylinder's volume. Cone Volume = (1/3) × π × r² × h.

Circumference and Area of Base

The base of a cylinder is a circle. Base Area = π × r² and Base Perimeter (Circumference) = 2 × π × r. The CSA can directly be calculated as Base Perimeter × height.

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questionText: A thief running at a speed of 8 km/h is chased by a policeman whose speed is 10 km/h. If the thief is 100 m ahead of the policeman, then the time required for the policeman to catch the thief will be:
solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Relative speed of policeman = 10 - 8 = 2 km/h
Distance gap to close = 100 m = 0.1 km
Time required = Distance ÷ Relative speed = 0.1 ÷ 2 = 1/20 hours
Time in minutes = 1/20 × 60 = 3 minutes
∴ The correct answer is 3 minutes.

Alternate Method
Given:
Speed of the policeman (Sp) = 10 km/h
Speed of the thief (St) = 8 km/h
Initial distance ahead (D) = 100 m = 0.1 km

Formula Used:
Relative Speed = Sp - St (Since they move in the same direction)
Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

Calculations:
⇒ Relative Speed = 10 - 8 = 2 km/h
⇒ Time required to catch the thief = 0.1 km ÷ 2 km/h = 0.05 hours
⇒ To convert hours into minutes, multiply by 60:
⇒ Time required = 0.05 × 60 = 3 minutes
∴ The correct answer is 3 minutes.

Additional Information
Relative Speed (Same Direction)

When two bodies move in the same direction at speeds S1 and S² (where S1 > S²), their relative speed is S1 - S².

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction)

When two bodies move towards each other at speeds S1 and S², their relative speed is S1 + S².

Speed Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply the speed by 5 ÷ 18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18 ÷ 5.
conceptTested: Time required to catch a moving target is the initial separation distance divided by the relative speed.
